how: UDisc lists four disc golf courses inside Chicago, including an 18-hole course at Jackson Park and 9-hole courses at Washington Park and Illinois Tech.
The Chicago Avenue Fire Arts Center teaches traditional blacksmithing and forging classes to the public.
ULAX Chicago runs recreational men's field lacrosse leagues for all skill levels at Clark Park and UIC turf, plus a winter box league.
The Palos Forest Preserves have 25+ miles of singletrack for all levels, staged from Maple Lake East Grove and maintained by CAMBr.
The City of Chicago Pipe Band runs an academy teaching bagpipes and drums to novices through competitive players.
Notes To Music School offers harp lessons at its North Side studio, in homes or online, and other Chicago teachers are listed on Lessons.com.
Chicago Model Masters, an AMA-chartered club, flies RC aircraft at Kickapoo Woods forest preserve in Riverdale; Palos R/C Flying Club flies at Morrill Meadows.
Artist Mami Takahashi teaches beginner kintsugi workshops at the International Museum of Surgical Science and the Japanese Culture Center.
Indigo & Violet Studio runs two-hour beginner macrame workshops (plant hanger, yoga strap) with materials included.
The Chopping Block teaches hands-on mozzarella and ricotta cheesemaking classes for adults.
Pacific College of Health and Science's Chicago campus hosts free qigong and taiji practice sessions open to anyone, and Chicago Tai Chi teaches qigong downtown.
Hampden Watch Company's First Hand workshop is a one-day class where up to six beginners assemble a Swiss 6498 movement.
Chicago Printmakers Collaborative teaches multi-session stone lithography courses for all levels.
Chicago Duplicate Bridge runs daytime and evening duplicate games at Century Mall, and other clubs meet at the Chicago Cultural Center and University Club.
Chris's Billiards, a long-running Northwest Side pool hall, has dozens of tables, and other halls (Red Shoe, Pressure Billiards, Southport Lanes) offer tables and leagues.
Lakeside Lawn Bowling Club plays on the public green in Jackson Park, with free lessons and club bowls for newcomers.
The Japanese Culture Center runs paper-folding workshops, and the Chicago Area Origami Society has held free open folding meetings at Garfield Park Conservatory.
Cozymeal and ClassBento list beginner chocolate-making classes (tempering, truffles, bars) with local chefs, but these are confection classes rather than bean-to-bar production.
Alliance Française de Chicago runs French classes for adults and kids across seven CEFR levels, on site, online and hybrid.

The Korean American Center offers King Sejong Institute-certified Korean courses for all ages, mainly live on Zoom, and Chicago Korean Education Center has held in-person adult classes at Hana Center.

activity: Magic: The Gathering and trading card games
how: Good Games Chicago hosts Magic: The Gathering, Pokemon and Lorcana events most nights in a 40+ seat play area, and Chicagoland Games (Dice Dojo) in Edgewater runs Magic prereleases and leagues.
Chicago Sake School runs small-group Sake for Beginners and Sake Immersion tasting classes, and restaurants such as Ani have hosted Sake 101 tastings.
Guides name Grant Park and the Chicago Riverwalk as the main downtown drone spots, but city rules restrict flying over people and property and sources disagree on what parks allow.
Shedd Aquarium and the Alliance for the Great Lakes run free volunteer beach cleanups and Adopt-A-Beach days on Chicago lakefront beaches such as 12th Street Beach.
Eat the Neighborhood and Foraging Walks - Chicago run guided wild-food foraging walks in city parks such as Montrose Bird Sanctuary and Winnemac Park.
Chicago Cycleboats runs 90-minute pedal-powered group boat tours on the Chicago River from the Riverwalk; self-drive pedal boats are at Independence Grove in Libertyville (about 55 km out).
The Chicago Genealogical Society offers research guides for Chicago, Cook County and Illinois, a family photo database and regular evening webinars.
